title: Goldstream Implementation Pulse — Ops & Security Intake
summary: Kickoff for implementation intake: discuss network connectivity (VPC, peering), data residency and retention, dedicated vs hosted options, pilot success criteria, and next steps including security docs and benchmark plan.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood); Aisha, Miguel, Claire, Tom (Goldstream)
Notes: recording auto transcript, occasional mis-hearings present

[00:00] Jordan Hayes: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time today, uh this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm AE on the account. we want to run through the implementation pulse, figure connectivity and security checks, and leave with clear next steps. priya will cover the technical checklist.

[00:18] Aisha Reynolds: thanks Jordan. morning from NY — quick intro, i'm Aisha, head of platform. Miguel is our devops lead, Claire on security, Tom is PM for the customer-facing features. we're targetting a pilot in mid-march so wanted to align on blockers.

[00:35] Priya Kapoor: hi team, priya here — i'll jump into the infra and runtime specifics. quick preface: Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated pools, and private (VPC/on-prem) deployments; we usually map pilots to hosted or dedicated depending on data sensitivity.

[01:05] Miguel Santos: question straight away — Goldstream has strict PII handling; can you summarize encryption at rest and key management? we run keys in AWS KMS.

[01:20] Priya Kapoor: yes — encrypted at rest by default, integrate with customer KMS for dedicated/private deployments. note: for hosted we have a customer-specific key option through a bring-your-key (BYK) flow, though the current hosted flow involves a managed key with strong separation. i'll send the exact KMS flow doc.

[01:42] Claire Ng: right — and audit logs? we need full request traces for a 12-month retention for compliance. does Redwood provide token-level logs and search?

[01:56] Jordan Hayes: short answer yes — our Console exposes per-token breakdowns, per-route latency and model traces, and we can extract audit logs to a supplied S3 bucket. retention windows are configurable per-customer. for dedicated/private you can have infinite retention in your own storage.

[02:20] Tom Becker: on the infra side, are we leaning dedicated or hosted for the pilot? cost and latency are both important — we'll demo end-user features to a subset of customers.

[02:35] Priya Kapoor: usually for a short pilot hosted is fastest — less networking. but if data residency or audit demands SSO/KMS integrations that we can't map to hosted in your region, dedicated or private might be required. given Claire's retention ask and KMS usage, dedicated looks likely unless you're comfortable with the hosted BYK option.

[03:05] Miguel Santos: network-wise: we want VPC peering and restricted egress. do you support AWS VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink?

[03:18] Priya Kapoor: both patterns are supported. PrivateLink is our preferred for production-grade private connectivity; VPC peering is supported for dedicated in certain regions. there's also a customer-managed control plane for private installs. i'll add a table of supported regions / connectivity patterns in the follow-up.

[03:42] Claire Ng: SSO — we run Okta. does Redwood support SAML & SCIM and role-based access? we need RBAC mapped to our Okta groups.

[03:55] Jordan Hayes: yes — SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning and RBAC is supported. for dedicated/private we can integrate directly. hosted can do SAML too, but provisioning via SCIM is most mature on dedicated. Priya: correct me if i'm wrong on the SCIM parity.

[04:15] Priya Kapoor: that's right — hosted supports SAML, dedicated has full SCIM + fine-grained RBAC controls. there are a couple of small differences around group sync timing, i'll document them.

[04:33] Aisha Reynolds: success criteria for the pilot: 1) integration complete with VPC or PrivateLink, 2) <200ms p95 generation for our short prompts, 3) data audit logs in our S3 with 12-month retention, 4) certification of encryption & SSO. is that reasonable?

[04:55] Jordan Hayes: that's a good initial set. quick note on the latency target — depends on batch sizes and model. if you need 200ms p95 on a high-capacity model we may recommend a smaller context model or dedicated pool sizing; we'll propose a benchmark matrix.

[05:15] Miguel Santos: we're testing two models: one for summaries and one for question-answering. the summary flow is long-context but fewer tokens; the QA is short but high qps. can Redwood handle mixed workloads in pilot?

[05:30] Priya Kapoor: yes — we can route by model and route. smart routing and autoscale let you pin certain traffic to dedicated pools and fallback to hosted variants. there's also prefix/KV caching for summary templates which could reduce cost and latency.

[05:55] Tom Becker: can we do a smoke benchmark before the pilot to verify tails and autoscale behavior?

[06:05] Jordan Hayes: absolutely — our SE team can run a 1-hour spike run using your prompt set. we'll need API keys and a minimal payload set. we usually run two passes: functional then load.

[06:20] Miguel Santos: how does cost attribution work? we want token-level cost breakdowns by route so product can see which features cost more.

[06:33] Priya Kapoor: Console provides token-level cost per request and you can tag routes. we'll show you tagging best practices. also Redwood Optimize can suggest batching or quantization to reduce unit cost.

[06:50] Claire Ng: any SOC2/ISO artifacts you can share now? also penetration test reports?

[07:00] Jordan Hayes: yes — i'll share our compliance pack (SOC 2, ISO summaries, penetration test redacted reports). there is a security folder link: https://redwood.example.com/security/goldstream-pack (link shared).

[07:18] Claire Ng: perfect. for hosted BYK, do we hold the master key or you do? we prefer customer-owned master key (we manage KMS).

[07:30] Priya Kapoor: dedicated and private allow full customer KMS control. hosted BYK has a hosted key option with customer-scoped encryption but not full HSM control in all regions. we'll map your region needs.

[07:50] Jordan Hayes: quick operational question — who at Goldstream will be the day-to-day contact for the pilot?

[08:00] Aisha Reynolds: miguel will be lead for infra, claire for security sign-off, tom for product acceptance. i'm the sponsor.

[08:12] Jordan Hayes: great. i'll summarize roles in the follow-up.

[08:20] Tom Becker: timeline — can we do smoke tests next week and have a pilot window 3/16–3/30?

[08:30] Priya Kapoor: timeline looks feasible. we'll need API credentials and a sample prompt set by Friday to do a proper smoke run. also a short runbook for PrivateLink/VPC setup.

[09:02] Miguel Santos: network prep: who creates peering connections? our infra team or your SRE?

[09:15] Priya Kapoor: usually customer infra initiates peering from their side; we'll provide the target endpoints and a step-by-step. for PrivateLink there are a few cross-account steps that our SREs can assist with.

[09:45] Jordan Hayes: ok — list of deliverables we'll own vs Goldstream: we'll own security pack, run smoke benchmarks, provide runbook. you own network peering and provide sample prompts/traffic.

[10:05] Claire Ng: can we get a data flow diagram? we need to show egress points and where logs land.

[10:18] Priya Kapoor: yes — we'll attach a diagram to the security pack.

[10:30] Aisha Reynolds: any gotchas around KV cache or session state? we use contextual state a lot.

[10:42] Priya Kapoor: KV cache is supported for long-lived sessions and can be stored in dedicated pools; some hosted models have limited KV windowing. i'll note exact per-model constraints.

[11:05] Tom Becker: procurement — is the pilot free trial or usage billed?

[11:18] Jordan Hayes: pilot terms are flexible; usually a combination: credits for baseline usage and overage billing. for enterprise we can agree a short reserved credit for dedicated pilots. procurement will follow — i'll loop in sales ops.

[11:45] Miguel Santos: competitor question — we've also discussed VendorX and BigCloud AI, curious how Redwood differs on observability and rollout controls.

[11:58] Jordan Hayes: differences: first-class per-route observability, token-level cost breakdowns, rollout policies like canary and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants. i'll share a short one-pager.

[12:18] Claire Ng: any additional compliance checks for EU residency? we may route EU users to EU region.

[12:30] Priya Kapoor: yes — regional model hosting and data residency are supported; we'll provide the region availability matrix. for EU tenancy we can pin model serving to eu-west data centers.

[12:55] Tom Becker: nice. i'm also interested in how model versioning works — we need to freeze a model for the pilot and be able to roll forward.

[13:08] Priya Kapoor: our platform supports model pinning per-route, controlled rollouts, and staged canary. we log evals and quality metrics tied to prompt sets so you can detect regressions.

[13:30] Aisha Reynolds: ok, let's recap and next steps, please.

[13:40] Jordan Hayes: recap: 1) Redwood to send security pack, KMS/BYK details, and region matrix (Priya) 2) Redwood SE to run smoke benchmark next week — needs sample prompts and API creds (Priya + SE team) 3) Goldstream to start VPC/PrivateLink prep and share point-of-contact (Miguel) 4) Goldstream security to review SOC2 and PT artifacts (Claire) 5) agree pilot contract terms and credits (Jordan + procurement).

[14:10] Miguel Santos: action: we'll aim to share prompt set and creds by Friday. Miguel will open a ticket for network peering.

[14:25] Claire Ng: action: security review — i'll review docs within 5 business days.

[14:35] Jordan Hayes: sounds great. i'll send notes and links, and schedule the smoke run for next Tuesday.

[14:50] Tom Becker: one more quick Q — how do we handle PII scrubbing before logs land?

[15:00] Priya Kapoor: we have optional pre-log scrubbing and field-level redaction hooks; for dedicated/private you can run scrubbing in your VPC prior to log export. we'll include config examples.

[15:20] Aisha Reynolds: thanks everyone — that was useful. we'll reconvene after the smoke run.

[15:30] Jordan Hayes: thanks team, meeting adjourned.

(Transcript auto-generated; may contain occasional mis-typed acronyms like "V-P-C" or "K-V cash")

Redwood SE Team; Schedule and run smoke benchmark (functional + load) next Tue; needs sample prompts and API creds; due 2026-02-17
Miguel Santos; Open network peering ticket and begin PrivateLink prep; due 2026-02-13
Claire Ng; Review SOC2 and pentest artifacts and provide feedback; due 2026-02-17
Jordan Hayes; Draft pilot commercial term sheet and share with procurement; due 2026-02-14

Goldstream to provide sample prompt set and API credentials by Friday
Schedule smoke benchmark for next Tuesday
Start VPC/PrivateLink network work and confirm point-of-contact
Agree pilot terms and credit structure with procurement
